🚨 FACTOR OPTIONS - "IV VIEW" LIVE on https://t.co/5ggAYZBa1M 🚨

Most tools are strictly backward looking and report the news...
what did this factor do during COVID? 
what did this pair do last month?

NOW you get a forward looking gauge to put next to your own view... the question we are trying to answer is... what do traders expect each factor to do over the next 30 days (+ 3 other important metrics for context)

HOW TO USE IT
Open the IV VIEW on the home screen. For every factor with enough option contract data, you see the move the market is pricing over the next 30 days. e.g. AI Power Demand priced for ±X% and Hypergrowth SaaS for ±Y% are very different bets at the same position size

Then check which way traders lean. Paying more for puts than calls? Crash protection unusually expensive? Is the priced move bigger or smaller than how the factor has actually been moving?

Hover over a factor name for a plain English read of all four metrics. More metrics coming 

WHY IT'S UNIQUE
Options trade on single stocks and a few ETFs, not on themes or factors. So we built the read from the option contracts on every stock inside each factor (~2,000 names), rolled up from contracts to stocks to factors and adjusted for how those stocks move together... this was/is an interesting math & compute exercise 

WHERE TO USE
1. Home screen
2. IV tab (desktop)
3. Hover on FACTOR NAME & metrics for more details

Explore it and tell me what we should add.. this is release 1 of 4 major upgrades we have coming the next 2 weeks... we are really excited to show you what we have been cookin' up...

items.text:
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, probably Elon (and I) - one giant AI syndicate, obviously acting in coordination.

At this point, the fact that all the major AI companies coordinate the launches of their frontier models barely even feels debatable.

Every major release involves an enormous amount of work: deploying the model, updating infrastructure, apps, extensions, integrations, everything. And yet all the big launches keep happening in clusters, often literally on the same day, with maybe a day of variance at most.

There is simply no world in which a company can pull off a completely uncoordinated full-scale launch a couple of hours after a competitor releases something.

“Hey, look! Dario just dropped Opus 5.5! Ship GPT-6 Sol and Luna!”

“But Sam, they’re not even fully…”

“SHIP THEM!”

“But the tests, the infra…”

“PRESS THE GODDAMN BUTTON!”

I seriously doubt that’s what’s happening.

The second thing is that there seems to be a very obvious, coordinated, managed shift in where the hate goes.

Claude Code was the first to really blow up and build a huge user base. But at some point, around spring this year, it became increasingly obvious that OpenAI’s models were simply smarter.

Codex worked better and more elegantly. It handled tasks cleanly, one-shotted fixes in minutes, while Opus could spend an hour digging through the codebase and still fail to fix the bug.

Codex started gaining popularity and users. Tibo was sent out among us handing out resets like hotcakes.

Everyone loved Codex. Claude Code was just… meh.

Then Fable launches, after months of Mythos speculation, while OpenAI releases the 5.6 lineup.

And from that point on, the hate toward OpenAI starts steadily increasing alongside a catastrophic collapse in Codex usage limits.

Everyone starts complaining about Codex. Everyone starts praising Claude because at least Claude has reasonable usage limits.

And OpenAI does basically NOTHING.

No public acknowledgment that their latest models can now vaporize your subscription allowance in a matter of hours.

Just the occasional Tibo post:

“We massively improved something, here’s another reset.”

They didn’t. In practice, it somehow gets worse every single week.

So right now, Codex is the antagonist: incredibly capable, but practically unusable because of the limits.

Claude Code is on top again: great models that you can actually use at reasonable volumes, even on a $20 subscription.

And again, all of this is happening while frontier model launches remain suspiciously coordinated.

What actually happens behind the scenes between the heads of these companies, and how exactly they coordinate their moves, I have no idea.

But to me, the pattern is becoming pretty damn hard to ignore.
